claim: 223 Arabidopsis thaliana accessions from the RegMap panel were used for genome-wide association studies.
source: A subset of 223 Arabidopsis thaliana accessions of the RegMap panel (Horton et al., 2012) was used for genome-wide association studies (Arabidopsis Biological Resource Center accession number CS77400).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states the number and source of accessions used.

claim: Zn deficiency in shoots of Col-0 plants was associated with the induction of ZIP4 and ZIP12 expression.
source: As expected, Zn deficiency in shoots of Col-0 plants was associated with the induction of the expression of two Zn-deficiency marker genes, ZIP4 and ZIP12 (Jain et al., 2013) (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1 and cited literature.

claim: Under +Zn condition, shoot Pi concentration varied across the 223 accessions from 3 to 10 μmol of Pi per gram of fresh weight with a median of ~5.45 μmol.gram−1 fresh weight of Pi.
source: Under the +Zn condition, shoot Pi concentration varied across the 223 accessions from 3 to 10 μmol of Pi per gram of fresh weight (median ~5.45 μmol.gram−1 fresh weight of Pi) (Figure 1—figure supplement 2A)
evidence: The claim is directly supported by measurements presented in the manuscript and shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2A.

claim: Under -Zn condition, shoot Pi concentration increased to 4–16 μmol of Pi per gram of fresh weight with a median of ~8.23 μmol.gram−1 fresh weight of Pi.
source: while in -Zn, it increased to 4–16 μmol of Pi per gram of fresh weight (median ~8.23 μmol.gram−1 fresh weight of Pi) (Figure 1—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: The claim is directly supported by measurements presented in the manuscript and shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2B.

claim: The broad-sense heritability (H2) of the shoot Pi concentrations was 0.63 under +Zn and 0.47 under –Zn conditions.
source: The broad-sense heritability (H2) of the shoot Pi concentrations was 0.63 and 0.47 under +Zn and –Zn conditions, respectively.
evidence: The heritability values are explicitly stated as calculated from the data.

claim: Using a 10% false discovery threshold, 13 significant SNPs in five distinct genomic loci were identified to be associated with Pi concentration in shoots, specific for the –Zn condition.
source: Using a non-conservative 10% false discovery threshold (FDR), we identified 13 significant SNPs in five distinct genomic loci to be associated with Pi concentration in the shoots, which was specific for the –Zn condition (Figure 1B).
evidence: The claim is supported by GWAS analysis results shown in Figure 1B.

claim: The most significantly associated SNP had a p-value of 5.86*10−8 and was located on Chromosome 1.
source: The most significantly associated SNP (p-value=5.86*10−8; FDR 1%) was located on Chromosome 1 (Supplementary file 2).
evidence: The p-value and chromosomal location are explicitly stated from GWAS results.

claim: The significantly associated SNP was located at the upstream and coding regions of At1g12640 and At1g12650.
source: The significantly associated SNP was located at the upstream and coding regions of two candidate genes, namely At1g12640 and At1g12650 (Figure 1D–E).
evidence: The genomic location is shown in Figure 1D-E.

claim: At1g12650 encodes an unknown protein likely to be involved in mRNA splicing via the spliceosome.
source: At1g12650 encodes an unknown protein likely to be involved in mRNA splicing via the spliceosome
evidence: The annotation is stated based on gene function prediction.

claim: At1g12640 encodes LysoPhosphatidylCholine AcylTransferase 1 (LPCAT1), a member of the Membrane Bound O-Acyl Transferase (MBOAT) gene family.
source: At1g12640 encodes a member of the Membrane Bound O-Acyl Transferase (MBOAT) gene family known as LysoPhosphatidylCholine AcylTransferase 1 (LPCAT1, [Wang et al., 2012]).
evidence: The gene identity is stated with citation to previous work.

claim: LPCAT1 is an evolutionarily conserved key enzyme involved in phospholipid metabolism and the Lands cycle.
source: LPCAT1 is an evolutionarily conserved key enzyme that is involved in phospholipid metabolism and more precisely in the Lands cycle (Lands, 1960).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to the Lands cycle literature.

claim: In Arabidopsis, LPCAT1 catalyzes the conversion of lysophosphatidylcholine (Lyso-PC) to produce phosphatidylcholine (PC).
source: In Arabidopsis LPCAT1 has been shown to catalyze the conversion of lysophosphatidylcholine (Lyso-PC) to produce phosphatidylcholine (PC) (Zheng et al., 2012).
evidence: The enzymatic function is stated with citation to previous work.

claim: In response to -Zn, Col-0 plants showed a significant increase (~29% increase, p-value<0.05) in their shoot Pi concentration compared to +Zn conditions.
source: In response to -Zn, Col-0 plants showed a significant increase (~29% increase, p-value<0.05) in their shoot Pi concentration compared to +Zn conditions (Figure 2A)
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental measurements shown in Figure 2A.

claim: lpcat1 mutants displayed a significant increase in shoot Pi concentration (~36% increase, p-value<0.05) in response to –Zn.
source: Importantly, while Pi accumulation in response to –Zn in At1g12650 mutants was indistinguishable from Col-0, lpcat1 mutants displayed a significant increase in shoot Pi concentration (~36% increase, p-value<0.05) (Figure 2A).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental measurements shown in Figure 2A.

claim: No significant differences in shoot Pi concentration were observed in lpcat1 mutants in the +Zn condition compared to Col-0.
source: We confirmed that this increase in shoot Pi concentration in the lpcat1 mutants is specific to the -Zn treatment as no significant differences were observed in the +Zn condition compared to Col-0.
evidence: The claim is based on experimental comparison between genotypes and conditions.

claim: LPCAT1, and not At1g12650, is involved in regulating shoot Pi concentration in response to Zn deficiency in Arabidopsis.
source: These results showed that LPCAT1, and not At1g12650, is involved in regulating shoot Pi concentration in response to Zn deficiency in Arabidopsis.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the differential phenotypes of the two mutants.

claim: A single copy of the 10 bp Zinc Deficiency Response Element (ZDRE, RTGTCGACAY) is present 377 bp upstream of the LPCAT1 start codon in Col-0.
source: We identified the presence of a single copy of the 10 bp Zinc Deficiency Response Element (ZDRE, RTGTCGACAY)(Assunção et al., 2010), located 377 bp upstream of the ATG (Figure 2B).
evidence: The claim is based on sequence analysis of the LPCAT1 promoter region.

claim: The ZDRE motif is a known binding site for the bZIP19 and bZIP23 transcription factors.
source: This motif is a known binding site for the bZIP19 and bZIP23 transcription factors, the key transcriptional regulators of the –Zn response (Assunção et al., 2010).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: Both bZIP19 and bZIP23 can bind to the ZDRE cis-regulatory element in the LPCAT1 promoter.
source: An electrophoretic mobility shift assay (EMSA) was performed, using a 30 bp promoter fragment containing the 10 bp potential ZDRE, which confirmed that both bZIP19 and bZIP23 could bind to this cis-regulatory element (Figure 2C)
evidence: The claim is supported by EMSA experimental results shown in Figure 2C.

claim: A new motif GTGTCGAA was identified in the 5' untranslated region of LPCAT1, similar to the ZDRE motif.
source: Further analysis of the regulatory regions of LPCAT1 led us to identify a new motif GTGTCGAA (5' untranslated region of LPCAT1), very similar to that of the ZDRE motif (RTGTCGACAY) (Figure 2B).
evidence: The claim is based on sequence analysis shown in Figure 2B.

claim: bZIP23 can bind to the newly identified motif GTGTCGAA, while bZIP19 showed extremely weak (if any) binding capacity.
source: Interestingly, EMSA analysis revealed that bZIP23 could bind to the newly identified motif, while bZIP19 showed an extremely weak (if any) binding capacity to new motif (Figure 2C).
evidence: The claim is supported by EMSA experimental results shown in Figure 2C.

claim: LPCAT1 transcript accumulation showed significant down-regulation in response to -Zn compared to +Zn conditions at 6, 12 and 18 days.
source: In response to -Zn, transcript accumulation of LPCAT1 was changed, showing significant down-regulation compared +Zn conditions (Figure 2D).
evidence: The claim is supported by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: LPCAT1 transcript was significantly up-regulated in the bzip23 and bzip19/bzip23 mutant lines compared to Col-0 and bzip19 in –Zn.
source: The LPCAT1 transcript was significantly up-regulated in the bzip23 and bzip19/bzip23 mutant lines, compared to Col-0 and bzip19 in –Zn, which showed a significant down-regulation (Figure 2D).
evidence: The claim is supported by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 2D (likely Figure 2E based on context).

claim: bZIP23, but not bZIP19, is involved in negatively regulating the expression of LPCAT1 under –Zn.
source: This indicates that bZIP23, but not bZIP19, is involved in negatively regulating the expression of LPCAT1 under –Zn.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the differential expression patterns in mutant backgrounds.

claim: bzip23 and bzip19/bzip23 mutants showed a significant decrease in shoot Pi content compared to Col-0 in –Zn.
source: While in +Zn, all plants showed similar shoot Pi content, we observed a significant decrease in shoot Pi content in the bzip23 and bzip19/bzip23 mutants compared to Col-0, confirming the regulatory role of bZIP23 and not bZIP19 (Figure 2E).
evidence: The claim is supported by Pi measurement data shown in Figure 2E (likely Figure 2F based on context).

claim: bZIP23 represses LPCAT1 upon –Zn, and this repression leads to the over-accumulation of Pi in shoots in Arabidopsis grown under –Zn condition.
source: Taken together, this suggests that bZIP23 represses LPCAT1 upon –Zn, and this repression leads to the over-accumulation of Pi in shoots in Arabidopsis grown under –Zn condition.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the combined genetic and molecular data.

claim: The common ZDRE motif did not display any variation between two groups of accessions with high and low Pi accumulation ratios.
source: Interestingly, comparative sequence analysis of the regulatory regions of LPCAT1 of these accessions using the sequence data from the 1001 genomes project (1001 Genomes Consortium, 2016) revealed that the common ZDRE motif (Figure 2B) didn't display any variation between these two groups of accession (Figure 3A)
evidence: The claim is based on sequence comparison analysis shown in Figure 3A.

claim: The newly identified bzip23 specific motif showed variation between two groups of accessions, with low Pi ratio accessions exhibiting GTGTCGAA and high Pi accumulating accessions displaying GTGTCACA.
source: and that the newly identified bzip23 specific motif (Figure 2B) showed clear variation between the two groups of accession with the accessions with low Pi ratio under -Zn exhibiting a Col-0 like GTGTCGAA motif and the high Pi accumulating accession displaying a GTGTCACA motif (Figure 3A, Figure 3—figure supplement 1, Supplementary file 3).
evidence: The claim is based on sequence comparison analysis shown in Figure 3A and supplementary data.

claim: Only bZIP23 could bind to the GTGTCACA version of the ZDRE motif.
source: EMSA analysis revealed that only bZIP23 could bind to this version of ZDRE motif (Figure 3B).
evidence: The claim is supported by EMSA experimental results shown in Figure 3B.

claim: bZIP23 acted as a stronger repressor of the LPCAT1 Col-0 mutated promoter containing the new ZDRE of Sap-0 compared to the Col-0 LPACT1 native promoter.
source: Consistent with the hypothesis that the natural variation of the new ZDRE is relevant for LPCAT1 regulation, bZIP23 acted as stronger repressor of the LPCAT1 Col-0 mutated promoter that contained the new ZDRE of Sap-0 compared to the Col-0 LPACT1 native promoter (Figure 3D).
evidence: The claim is supported by in planta transactivation assay results shown in Figure 3D.

claim: LPCAT1 was downregulated by a larger extent in accessions that accumulated more Pi upon –Zn and contained the new (non Col-0) ZDRE.
source: Moreover, LPCAT1 was downregulated by a larger extent in accessions that accumulated more Pi upon –Zn (Figure 3E) and contained the new (non Col-0) ZDRE
evidence: The claim is supported by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 3E.

claim: The expression of bZIP23 remained unchanged in all accessions and growth conditions tested.
source: while the expression of bZIP23 remained unchanged in all accessions and growth conditions tested.
evidence: The claim is based on gene expression analysis across conditions.

claim: The LPCAT1 promoter and predicted amino acid coding sequences of Col-0 and Sap-0 displayed 97.9% and 99.4% sequence identity respectively.
source: Noteworthy, the LPCAT1 promoter and predicted amino acid coding sequences of Col-0 and Sap-0 displayed 97.9% and 99.4% sequence identity respectively (data not shown).
evidence: The claim is based on sequence comparison analysis.

claim: When expressed under the pLPCAT1Col-0 promoter, LPCAT1Col-0 or LPCAT1Sap-0 complemented the lpcat1-1 knock-out mutant phenotype and showed similar Pi content to WT (Col-0) plants in both +Zn and –Zn conditions.
source: When expressed under the pLPCAT1Col-0 promoter, LPCAT1Col-0 or LPCAT1Sap-0 complemented the lpcat1-1 knock-out mutant phenotype and showed a similar Pi content to WT (Col-0) plants in both +Zn and –Zn conditions (Figure 4B).
evidence: The claim is supported by complementation experiment data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: Lines complemented with the pLPCAT1Sap-0:LPCAT1Col-0 or pLPCAT1Sap-0:LPCAT1Sap-0 transgenic lines showed significantly higher Pi content compared to pLPCAT1Col-0:LPCAT1Col-0 or pLPCAT1Col-0:LPCAT1Sap-0 lines or WT (Col-0) in -Zn conditions.
source: In contrast, lines complemented with the pLPCAT1Sap-0:LPCAT1Col-0 or pLPCAT1Sap-0:LPCAT1Sap-0 transgenic lines showed significantly higher Pi content compared to pLPCAT1Col-0:LPCAT1Col-0 or pLPCAT1Col-0:LPCAT1Sap-0 lines or WT (Col-0) in -Zn conditions (Figure 4B).
evidence: The claim is supported by complementation experiment data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: Regulatory variation in the LPCAT1 promoter determines Pi accumulation.
source: This result demonstrates that regulatory variation in of the LPCAT1 promotor determines Pi accumulation
evidence: The claim is inferred from the complementation experiments showing promoter-dependent effects.

claim: Lines complemented with LPCAT1 driven by pLPCAT1 Sap-0 accumulate significantly lower LPCAT1 mRNA than those under the control of pLPCAT1 Col-0 and WT (Col-0) under –Zn.
source: Our result showed that while LPCAT1 is down-regulated in all tested lines by –Zn treatments, the lines complemented with the LPCAT1 driven by pLPCAT1 Sap-0 accumulates significantly lower LPCAT1 mRNA than that of those under the control of pLPCAT1 Col-0 and WT (Col-0) (Figure 4C).
evidence: The claim is supported by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: The allelic variation between Col-0 and Sap-0 in the promoter of the LPCAT1 gene causes the difference in LPCAT1 expression and leads to the difference in Pi accumulation under –Zn.
source: Taken together, our results indicate that the allelic variation between Col-0 and Sap-0 in the promoter of the LPCAT1 gene causes the difference in LPCAT1 expression, and confirm that this difference leads to the difference in Pi accumulation under –Zn.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the combined complementation and expression data.

claim: LPCAT1 catalyzes the conversion of lyso-phosphatidylcholine (Lyso-PC) to phosphatidylcholine (PC) in the remodelling pathway of PC biosynthesis.
source: While LPCAT1 had not been implicated in any known process involving Zn, it is known to catalyse the conversion of lyso-phosphatidylcholine (Lyso-PC) to phosphatidylcholine (PC) in the remodelling pathway of PC biosynthesis (Figure 5A) (Lands, 1960; Chen et al., 2007; Wang et al., 2012).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous work and shown in Figure 5A.

claim: In +Zn, no significant changes in the Lyso-PC and PC levels in Col-0, bzip23, and lpcat1 mutants were observed.
source: In +Zn, no significant changes in the Lyso-PC and PC levels in the three different genotypes were observed (Figure 5B,C).
evidence: The claim is supported by phospholipid measurement data shown in Figure 5B,C.

claim: Under –Zn, bzip23 showed a modest (but non-significant) decrease in the Lyso-PC/PC ratio.
source: However, under –Zn, bzip23 showed a modest (but non-significant) decrease in the Lyso-PC/PC ratio
evidence: The claim is based on phospholipid ratio measurements.

claim: Under –Zn, mutation in LPCAT1 resulted in a significant increase of Lyso-PC and a decrease of PC, resulting in an increase of the Lyso-PC/PC ratio (~1.2 fold, p-value<0.05) compared to Col-0 plants.
source: while the mutation in LPCAT1 resulted in a significant increase of Lyso-PC and a decrease of PC, resulting in an increase of the Lyso-PC/PC ratio (~1.2 fold, p-value<0.05) compared to Col-0 plants (Figure 5D).
evidence: The claim is supported by phospholipid measurement data shown in Figure 5D.

claim: LPCAT1 function is required to maintain the shoot Lyso-PC/PC ratio under –Zn.
source: These results demonstrate that the LPCAT1 function is required to maintain the shoot Lyso-PC/PC ratio under –Zn.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the altered phospholipid ratios in lpcat1 mutants.

claim: Under –Zn conditions, Sap-0, pLPCAT1Sap-0::LPCAT1Col-0, pLPCAT1Sap-0::LPCAT1Sap-0 or lpcat1 lines showed a significant decrease of PC and increase of LPC concentrations, leading to an increase of Lyso-PC/PC ratios.
source: However, under –Zn conditions, Sap-0, pLPCAT1Sap-0::LPCAT1Col-0, pLPCAT1Sap-0::LPCAT1Sap-0 or lpcat1 lines showed a significant decrease of PC and increase of LPC concentrations, leading to an increase of Lyso-PC/PC ratios (Figure 6).
evidence: The claim is supported by phospholipid measurement data shown in Figure 6.

claim: The third most significant associated peak (8% FDR) under –Zn conditions was located in a region of chromosome 5 containing PHT1;1, PHT1;2, PHT1;3 and PHT1;6 genes.
source: The third most significant associated peak (8% FDR) under –Zn conditions was located in a region of chromosome 5 containing members of the high affinity Pi transporters PHT1 gene family, namely PHT1;1, PHT1;2, PHT1;3 and PHT1;6 (Chr5 : 17394363–174200000) (Figure 7A–C, Supplementary file 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by GWAS analysis results shown in Figure 7A-C.

claim: PHT1;1 was the only member of the PHT1 gene family to be significantly up-regulated in the -Zn condition in all genotypes.
source: In all genotypes, PHT1;1 was the only member of the PHT1 gene family to be significantly up-regulated in the -Zn condition (Figure 7D).
evidence: The claim is supported by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 7D.

claim: Zn deficiency induces transcription of PHT1;1 by ~2.2 fold (p<0.05) in WT (Col-0), and this induction was further increased by 2-fold (p<0.01) in lpcat1 mutants.
source: Zn deficiency induces transcription of PHT1;1 already ~2.2 fold (p<0.05) in WT (Col-0), and this induction was further increased by 2-fold (p<0.01) in lpcat1 mutants (Figure 7D), when compared to +Zn (Figure 7—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 7D and Figure 7—figure supplement 1.

claim: The pht1;1 mutant showed low Pi accumulation in presence of Zn compared to WT plants.
source: The pht1;1 mutant showed low Pi accumulation in presence of Zn compared to WT plants (Figure 7E) consistently with (Shin et al., 2004) that reported that the pht1;1 mutant showed a reduction in Pi content of the shoots relative to wild type plants grown under control condition (+Pi + Zn).
evidence: The claim is supported by Pi measurement data shown in Figure 7E and cited literature.

claim: No increase of Pi concentration was observed in the shoots of pht1;1 grown in -Zn.
source: Importantly, no increase of Pi concentration was observed in the shoots of pht1;1 grown in -Zn, which contrast with the Pi accumulation in pht1;2 and pht1;3 that was in a similar range to WT plants in presence or absence of Zn.
evidence: The claim is based on Pi measurement data comparing mutants and conditions.

claim: PHT1;1 is involved in the overaccumulation of Pi in the shoot of lpcat1 grown in -Zn.
source: These results show the involvement of PHT1;1 in the overaccumulation of Pi in the shoot of lpcat1 grown in -Zn
evidence: The claim is inferred from the genetic analysis of pht1;1 mutant phenotype.

claim: Zn deprivation causes an up-regulation of PHT1;1 and consequently an over-accumulation of Pi in Arabidopsis thaliana.
source: For instance, Zn deprivation causes an up-regulation of PHT1;1 and consequently an over-accumulation of Pi in Arabidopsis thaliana (Jain et al., 2013; Khan et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: The Zn deficiency-induced Pi uptake transporter expression is independent of the canonical 'PHR1-miR399-PHO2' signalling pathway.
source: Remarkably, although the involvement of PHOSPHATE RESPONSE1 transcription factor (PHR1) in the coordination of Pi-Zn homeostasis has been demonstrated (Khan et al., 2014), the Zn deficiency-induced Pi uptake transporter expression is independent of the aforementioned canonical 'PHR1-miR399-PHO2' signalling pathway (Khan et al., 2014)
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: About 800,000 child deaths per year are attributable to Zn deficiency alone according to the World Health Organization.
source: According to the World Health Organization, about 800,000 child deaths per year are attributable to Zn deficiency alone (Akhtar, 2013).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to WHO data.

claim: Zn and iron (Fe) deficiencies affect up to 2 billion people worldwide.
source: In particular, zinc (Zn) and iron (Fe) deficiencies affect up to 2 billion people worldwide (Hilty et al., 2010).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to epidemiological data.

claim: When the Zn supply is low, increasing P supply causes a reduction of plant height, delayed development and severe leaf symptoms including chlorosis and necrosis.
source: Noteworthy, when the Zn supply is low, increasing P supply causes a reduction of plant height, delayed development and severe leaf symptoms including chlorosis and necrosis (Ova et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: At high P supplies, Zn deficiency associated with elevated shoot P levels causes P toxicity.
source: At high P supplies, Zn deficiency associated with elevated shoot P levels causes P toxicity (Marschner, 2012).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: P-Zn interaction is recognized in a wide variety of biological systems, including rats, human cells, and multiple fungal species.
source: Interestingly, this P-Zn interaction is also recognized in a wide variety of other biological systems, including rats (Wallwork et al., 1983), human cells (Sandström and Lönnerdal, 1989), and multiple fungal species (Freimoser et al., 2006).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous work in different organisms.

claim: In Saccharomyces cerevisiae yeast, the Zn status acts as a major determinant of the ability to store P.
source: In Saccharomyces cerevisiae yeast, the Zn status acts as a major determinant of the ability to store P (Simm et al., 2007).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to previous work in yeast.

claim: World-wide P reserves are becoming increasingly scarce and a potential P crisis looms for agriculture at the end of the 21st century.
source: At the same time, world-wide P reserves are becoming increasingly scarce and a potential P crisis looms for agriculture at the end of this 21 st century (Abelson, 1999; Neset and Cordell, 2012).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous work on P resources.

claim: P is a critical component of many metabolites and macromolecules, including nucleic acids and phospholipids.
source: P is a critical component of many metabolites and macromolecules, including nucleic acids and phospholipids (PLs) (Poirier and Bucher, 2002; Rouached et al., 2010).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous work and represents established knowledge.

claim: Zn provides chemical, structural and regulatory functions in biological systems, for instance as cofactor for hundreds of enzymes, or by binding to PLs to maintain membrane structure.
source: Of equal importance, Zn provides chemical, structural and regulatory functions in biological systems (Christianson, 1991), for instance as cofactor for hundreds of enzymes, or by binding to PLs to maintain membrane structure (Binder et al., 2001; Sinclair and Krämer, 2012).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous work and represents established knowledge.

claim: In Arabidopsis thaliana, Pi uptake relies on members of the high affinity Pi transporter family (PHT1), of which PHT1;1 is the major contributor.
source: In Arabidopsis thaliana (Arabidopsis), this uptake relies on members of the high affinity Pi transporter family (PHT1) (Nussaume et al., 2011), of which PHT1;1 is the major contributor (Ayadi et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Upon P deficiency, the expression of some PHT1 transporters increases as a result of the activation of the 'PHR1-miR399-PHO2' signalling pathway.
source: Upon P deficiency, the expression of some PHT1 transporters increases as a result of the activation of the 'PHR1-miR399-PHO2' signalling pathway (Bari et al., 2006; Lin et al., 2008; Pant et al., 2008)
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: bZIP19 and bZIP23 are two essential members of the bZIP transcription factor family in Arabidopsis, without which plants are unable to respond to Zn starvation by inducing the expression of genes involved in Zn uptake and distribution such as ZIP4.
source: A putative working model of Zn deficiency signalling was proposed by Assunção et al. (2013), which is centred around two essential members of the bZIP transcription factor (TF) family in Arabidopsis, bZIP19 and bZIP23, without which plants are unable to respond to Zn starvation by inducing the expression of genes involved in Zn uptake and distribution such as the zinc transporter ZIP4 (Assunção et al., 2010).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Beyond common set of genes targeted by bZIP19 and bZIP23, each TF could regulate distinct genes.
source: Beyond common set of genes targeted by these two TFs, each TF could regulate distinct genes (Inaba et al., 2015)
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: CaMV 35S promoter driven overexpression of PHT1;1 significantly increases shoot Pi concentration.
source: The increase in PHT1;1 expression levels is likely to explain the increased shoot Pi concentration in lpcat1 since it is known that CaMV 35S promoter driven overexpression of this Pi transporter significantly increases shoot Pi concentration (Mitsukawa et al., 1997; Shin et al., 2004; Catarecha et al., 2007).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Lyso-PC acts as a signal for the regulation of the expression of arbuscular mycorrhiza (AM)-specific Pi transporter genes in potato, tomato and Lotus japonicus.
source: For instance, Lyso-PC was shown to act as a signal for the regulation of the expression of arbuscular mycorrhiza (AM)-specific Pi transporter genes in potato, tomato and recently in Lotus japonicus (Drissner et al., 2007; Vijayakumar et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: In Arabidopsis, alteration of the Lyso-PC/PC ratio shortens the time to flower.
source: For instance, in Arabidopsis alteration of the Lyso-PC/PC ratio shortens the time to flower (Nakamura et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: In human cells, the Lyso-PC/PC ratio was associated with an impairment of cell function, signalling and metabolism.
source: In human cells, the Lyso-PC/PC ratio was also associated with an impairment of cell function, signalling and metabolism (Mulder et al., 2003; Klavins et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: This study uncovered a novel pathway in which LPCAT1 plays a key role in the coordination of Pi homeostasis and Zn deficiency response in plants through modulation of phospholipid metabolism and Pi transporter expression.
source: Overall, this study uncovered a novel pathway, in which LPCAT1 plays a key role in the coordination of Pi homeostasis and Zn deficiency response in plants through modulation of phospholipid metabolism and Pi transporter expression.
evidence: The claim summarizes the main findings of the study.

claim: A complete pathway involved in the regulation of shoot Pi accumulation in –Zn can be defined as bZIP23-LPCAT1(Lyso-PC/PC)-PHT1;1.
source: By combining GWAS and functional genomics approaches, we discovered a complete pathway involved in the regulation of shoot Pi accumulation in –Zn that can be defined as bZIP23-LPCAT1(Lyso-PC/PC)-PHT1;1.
evidence: The claim summarizes the pathway discovered in the study.
